audit_findings.title: Nonrecurring ventilator buyback may inflate the FY2025 OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.239 million disposal gain and $16.151 million sale proceeds; 16.7% and 120.5% of the $13.4 million anchor, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained disposal gain increases normalized OE, while netting exceptional sale proceeds against property purchases understates recurring capital expenditure; either error is capitalized throughout the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: The ventilator buyback program was substantially completed as of December 31, 2025, and accordingly we do not expect additional material gains from these transactions in future periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurrence is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE worksheet removed both effects. The filed amounts are large relative to the anchor, particularly the proceeds, so their inclusion is reasonably capable of changing the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace FY2025 OE line by line; reverse the disposal gain with its tax effect, exclude all buyback proceeds, use gross property purchases when estimating recurring capital needs, and rerun every scenario if either item remains.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains only a partial year of the Lehan acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified OE; approximately $14.3 million of FY2025 revenue was included for six months
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE numerator includes only post-July 1 Lehan operations even though the valuation covers the entire acquired business.
audit_findings.evidence: The results of Lehan’s operations have been included in the Company’s consolidated financial statements since the date of acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated and understates run-rate OE, but its filed scale cannot reasonably reverse the conclusion. The market-price equity value is approximately $371.9 million versus the $233 million bull value, a $138.9 million gap. At the bull operating-value multiple of 16.57 times anchor OE, closing that gap would require about $8.38 million of additional OE. That equals 58.5% of Lehan's approximately $14.3 million six-month revenue contribution, exceeding the consolidated 57.5% gross margin before SG&A, taxes, and capital expenditure.
audit_findings.action: Normalize Lehan to a full year using its post-acquisition revenue, operating costs, taxes, interest, and required capital expenditure, then rerun for accuracy even though the correction is not capable of reversing the stated valuation conclusion.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition contingent consideration is a senior cash claim omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.750 million, or approximately $0.043 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The outstanding acquisition payment is a senior claim that should be deducted in the equity bridge unless its settlement is already charged to forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, contingent consideration liabilities of $ 1.8 million were included in accrued liabilities in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission: the June 30, 2026 filing confirms the full $1.750 million remained outstanding. Deducting it would reduce the $4.15-$5.68 scenario range by only about $0.043 per share, far smaller than the $3.40 gap between the $5.68 bull value and the $9.08 market price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct $1.750 million from each scenario's equity bridge and recompute per-share values, unless the model documents an explicit OE cash-flow charge for settlement.

audit_findings.title: Recurring fleet investment may be understated
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified maintenance requirement; FY2025 gross purchases were $39.985 million versus $23.834 million after $16.151 million of sale proceeds
audit_findings.mechanism: Underestimated maintenance and replacement capital directly overstates OE; omitted investment needed to support growth also overstates projected OE in the base and bull cases.
audit_findings.evidence: Purchases of property and equipment were primarily related to medical equipment placed with patients under our rental arrangements.
audit_findings.explanation: No demonstrated maintenance-capex error can be established without the worksheet and fleet data. The possibility is nevertheless material because gross FY2025 equipment purchases were nearly three times the $13.4 million OE anchor, and the $16.151 million difference between gross and net expenditure exceeded the anchor. A materially incorrect recurring-capital allocation could therefore change the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct maintenance capital from fleet age, useful lives, replacements, losses, damage, technology changes, patient placements, and ordinary disposal recoveries; separate growth capital consistently and rerun all scenarios with the normalized requirement.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 ventilator coverage rule may make FY2025 an unrepresentative base year
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; ventilator rentals were $136.749 million or 50.6% of FY2025 revenue and $71.771 million or 46.8% of first-half 2026 revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: Lower eligibility, authorization rates, reimbursement, utilization, or margins would reduce sustainable anchor OE and could invalidate the flat-to-positive growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: The final NCD may significantly affect patient access, reimbursement, and utilization of ventilator therapies.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved policy-impact possibility, not a demonstrated decline. First-half 2026 ventilator revenue rose 8.8% year over year and quarter-end ventilator patients increased from 12,152 to 12,635, but these figures do not establish claims acceptance, reimbursement realization, or steady-state margins. Because nearly half of revenue remains exposed, a sustained adverse effect is reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Analyze post-NCD claims approvals, denials, authorizations, patient starts and removals, realized reimbursement, collections, and contribution margins through the latest quarter; normalize OE and rerun scenarios if deterioration is identified.

audit_findings.title: Recorded equity investments are absent from the stakes bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $3.184 million carrying value, or approximately $0.078 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: If separable and investment income was purged from OE, the supportable realizable value belongs in the stakes bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The balance of the Company’s equity investments was $ 2.8 million as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The zero bridge entry is inconsistent with the filed $3.184 million investment balance, although recoverability and operating classification remain unresolved. Even adding the entire carrying amount would increase per-share value by only about $0.078 and the bull value from $5.68 to approximately $5.76, still well below the $9.08 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each June 30, 2026 investment, classify operating versus separable holdings, document recoverability, and add only the supported net realizable value to the bridge.
